defects: Unexplained additional image findings: ["The calcifications bilaterally are coarse, branching, dendritic/staghorn-pattern filling the pelvi-calyceal system, not the fine stippled medullary calcification expected for nephrocalcinosis; this pattern is more consistent with bilateral staghorn nephrolithiasis"]

findings: Anteroposterior projection of the abdomen and lower chest, supine positioning

Bilateral renal regions demonstrate multiple branching, arborizing, coarse calcifications with a dendritic/coral-like morphology occupying the collecting systems bilaterally, consistent with bilateral staghorn or partial staghorn calculi
The calcifications are dense, white, and branch in a pattern conforming to the renal pelvis and calyces bilaterally
The lumbar spine is visible centrally with maintained vertebral body heights and disc spaces
Gas is seen throughout the large and small bowel in a non-obstructive pattern
A large gas-filled structure is visible in the left upper quadrant, likely gastric fundus or splenic flexure
The pelvis is partially included; iliac wings are symmetric
No free intraperitoneal air is identified on this supine view
No obvious soft tissue masses or organomegaly clearly delineated
No vascular calcifications or pelvic phleboliths identified on this view
differential: Bilateral staghorn nephrolithiasis (struvite or calcium phosphate calculi filling the renal collecting systems bilaterally)
Bilateral medullary sponge kidney with nephrocalcinosis (medullary calcifications, though distribution here appears more pelvi-calyceal than medullary)
Bilateral renal tuberculosis with dystrophic calcification (though calcifications here appear intraluminal/collecting system rather than parenchymal)
anatomyConcerns: The upper chest and diaphragm are not fully included, limiting assessment of lower lung fields
Supine projection limits detection of free air or air-fluid levels; erect or decubitus views would be complementary
Image collimation cuts off the upper abdomen slightly on the right, potentially obscuring right hepatic margin
